data.enable_container_devices: Show Docker containers as separate devices
data.enable_nic_devices: Show network cards as separate devices
data.enable_hwmon_devices: Show USB sensor controllers as separate devices
data.enable_vm_devices: Show virtual machines as separate devices
data.enable_zfs_pool_devices: Show ZFS pools as separate devices

data_description.enable_container_updates: Periodically check Docker containers for available image updates. This may slow down polling and use additional network requests. Also creates an update entity for each container, from which its image update can be installed.
data_description.enable_fan_control: Create fan speed sensor and control entities. Disable if your system does not have controllable fans.
data_description.read_only: Only create sensors. Switches, buttons, and number controls are not created (existing ones are removed), and the integration's actions refuse to run, so Home Assistant cannot start, stop, or reboot anything on the server. Update entities still show available updates but do not offer to install them.
data_description.enable_websocket: WebSocket provides instant updates instead of polling. When disabled, data is polled every 30 seconds.
data_description.enable_container_devices: Give each container its own device under the server's Docker device, holding its switches, restart button, and metric sensors with short names (Running, CPU, Memory). When off, container entities stay on the server device, named after the container.
data_description.enable_gpu_devices: Give each GPU its own device under the server, holding its utilization, temperature, power, energy, and VRAM sensors with short names. When off, GPU sensors stay on the server device, named after the GPU.
data_description.enable_nic_devices: Give each PCI network card its own device under the server, with its ASIC, PHY, and MAC temperatures, and per port the link speed and the plugged optic's diagnostics (module temperature and voltage, RX and TX power, alarm and warning flags, vendor and part number). Needs an agent that reports network cards. When off, no network card entities are created (existing ones are removed).
data_description.enable_hwmon_devices: Give each USB sensor controller the agent identifies (for example an Aquacomputer Octo) its own device under the server, holding its fan and temperature sensors named by their lm-sensors labels ("Array Fan1", "Coolant Temp"). Entity IDs are kept. When off, these sensors stay on the server device. A channel labelled as flow in sensors.conf ("Coolant Flow") is shown as a flow channel either way; it still reports RPM.
data_description.enable_vm_devices: Give each VM its own device under the server's VMs device, holding its power switch, control buttons, and metric sensors (CPU, memory, network, and disk rates). When off, VM switches and buttons stay on the server device, and no VM sensors are created.
data_description.enable_zfs_pool_devices: Give each ZFS pool its own device under the server, holding its usage, health, scrub, and error sensors with short names, plus drive health roll-ups: hottest drive temperature, worst NVMe wear, media errors, failing drives, and a drive count with per-drive details. Drive health needs agent 2026.10 or later. When off, pool entities stay on the server device, named after the pool.

connection_failed.title: Connection to Unraid Server Failed
connection_failed.description:
Failed to connect to Unraid server at {host}:{port}.

Error: {error}

**Troubleshooting Steps:**
1. Verify the Unraid server is running
2. Check the host and port are correct
3. Ensure the Unraid Management Agent daemon is running
4. Check firewall settings
5. Verify network connectivity

Click Submit to acknowledge this issue.

disk_smart_errors.title: Disk SMART Errors Detected
disk_smart_errors.description:
Disk **{disk_name}** has {smart_errors} SMART errors.

SMART Status: {smart_status}

**Recommended Actions:**
1. Back up important data immediately
2. Run a full SMART test
3. Consider replacing the disk
4. Monitor disk health closely

disk_critical_temperature.title: Disk Critical Temperature
disk_critical_temperature.description:
Disk **{disk_name}** temperature is {temperature}°C (critical threshold: {threshold}°C).

⚠️ **URGENT - Immediate action required!**

**Recommended Actions:**
1. Consider spinning down the disk immediately
2. Check cooling/airflow in the system urgently
3. Verify all fans are operational
4. Improve ventilation or add cooling
5. Back up important data as a precaution

Click Submit to acknowledge this issue.

share_fuse_fallback.title: Share {share_name} is not using exclusive access

share_fuse_fallback_stray_unchecked.title: Share {share_name} is not using exclusive access
share_fuse_fallback_stray_unchecked.description:
Share **{share_name}** is set to live only on pool **{pool}**, but Unraid is serving it through the slower FUSE user share layer (`/mnt/user`) instead of exclusive access, because a `{share_name}` folder also exists on: **{locations}**. The agent did not check these spun-down disks or pools, to avoid waking them, so one may exist there too: **{unchecked}**.

**To fix:**
1. Check the `{share_name}` folder on {locations} (it may hold data) and move its contents to pool {pool}
2. Look for a `{share_name}` folder on {unchecked} and do the same
3. Remove the folders outside pool {pool}
4. Stop and start the array so Unraid switches the share back to exclusive access

This issue clears automatically once the share is exclusive again.

share_fuse_fallback_unchecked.title: Share {share_name} is not using exclusive access
share_fuse_fallback_unchecked.description:
Share **{share_name}** is set to live only on pool **{pool}**, but Unraid is serving it through the slower FUSE user share layer (`/mnt/user`) instead of exclusive access.

No `{share_name}` folder was found outside pool {pool} on the disks and pools that are awake. The agent did not check these spun-down disks or pools, to avoid waking them: **{unchecked}**. Look for a `{share_name}` folder there, move its contents to pool {pool} and remove it. Unraid decides exclusive access when the array starts, so stop and start the array afterwards.

This issue clears automatically once the share is exclusive again.

share_fuse_fallback_restart.title: Share {share_name} is not using exclusive access
share_fuse_fallback_restart.description:
Share **{share_name}** is set to live only on pool **{pool}**, but Unraid is serving it through the slower FUSE user share layer (`/mnt/user`) instead of exclusive access.

The agent found no `{share_name}` folder outside pool {pool}. Unraid decides exclusive access when the array starts, so if a stray folder was removed since then, stop and start the array.

This issue clears automatically once the share is exclusive again.

share_fuse_fallback_unknown.title: Share {share_name} is not using exclusive access
share_fuse_fallback_unknown.description:
Share **{share_name}** is set to live only on pool **{pool}**, but Unraid is serving it through the slower FUSE user share layer (`/mnt/user`) instead of exclusive access.

This usually means a `{share_name}` folder also exists on another disk or pool. The agent could not check where, so look for one outside pool {pool}, move its contents to pool {pool} and remove it, then stop and start the array.

This issue clears automatically once the share is exclusive again.
